statement: Finite exact-integer comparison only; no asymptotic inference.

normalization.frequency_support: odd h only, 1<=|h|<=H, because beta_h=0 for even h
normalization.raw_count: number of ordered (h1,d1,...,h4,d4) tuples on coefficient-compatible odd support

scales.label: D=X^(1/4)
scales.H_rule: nearest integer to D/X^(1/4), ties upward

brute_force_verification.method: literal Cartesian enumeration independent of the pair join

scales.label: D=round(X^(3/8))
scales.H_rule: nearest integer to D/X^(1/4), ties upward

brute_force_verification.method: literal Cartesian enumeration independent of the pair join

scales.label: D=X^(1/2)
scales.H_rule: nearest integer to D/X^(1/4), ties upward

brute_force_verification.method: omitted at endpoint to keep the diagnostic bounded

raw_vs_weighted.rule: At the endpoint natural band, exact reciprocal mass is strictly below the odd-supported raw count.

signed_vs_unsigned.rule: At the endpoint natural band, true signed mass is strictly below unsigned beta mass; triangle inequality holds in every band.

dyadic_endpoints.rule: The exact D=X^(1/4), rounded D=X^(3/8), and exact D=X^(1/2) rows all ran and include their natural nonzero bands.

real_vs_complex_pairing.rule: Raw=cosine pairing for shared weights; Re(B_h) only for real weights; asymmetric h-weights break symmetric pairing.

exact_vs_near.rule: N=0 and 0<|N| bands are accumulated in disjoint exact-integer tensors.

precision.rule: All beta masses agree at 50 and 80 digits to relative error below 1e-40.

small_scale_brute_force.rule: The independent literal enumeration exactly matches every pair-join tensor at the lower and crossover scales.

limitations: One bounded instance X=625 is used; there is no size sweep or exponent fit.
Sharp unit denominator weights are used for mass enumeration; smooth-weight behavior is not tested.
The raw count is coefficient-compatible (odd frequencies only), not an all-frequency count.
Only exact N=0 and cumulative bands |N|<=1, floor(D^4/X), and four times that natural band are tested.
The finite comparison cannot certify a uniform asymptotic bound or a crossover exponent.
